reviewer: Main integration; independent source-mapping review: OAuthMappingReview
resign-reason: The 2026-09-22 source walk retains direct mappings for the absolute-URI and fragment requirements. The historical increase in exclusions treated a retained request-parameter obligation as an applicability exclusion; source provenance now remains mapped while the summary preserves the owner's 2026-09-21 absent-request-feature decision. The remaining exclusions concern front-matter licensing, an introductory security assumption and an explicitly cited RFC 6749 obligation. The historical audience ids RFC8707-5-1 and RFC8707-5-2 state RFC 7519 Section 4.1.3 and were retired under owner decision D-10 (rfc/corrections/rfc8707.md). The bounded 2026-09-22 independent review accepted those mappings and annotations, without completing signing or proving implementation behaviour. The new RFC8707-2-4 citation correction needs review by Thomas or an independently assigned RFC reviewer before re-signing; this file carries no signature. Current source mappings were independently reviewed on 2026-09-22. This records the extraction mapping, not runtime conformance. Refreshed 2026-09-27 after that retirement: with two gated rows left the source derives its capitalised-keyword sites only, so the three lowercase sites (front:1, 1:1, 2.2:1, each excluded before) no longer derive; every remaining decision carried forward.

sections.reason: Section 2 states the SHOULD audience-restriction rule under historical RFC8707-3-1, the SHOULD NOT query-component rule under RFC8707-2-2, and the MAY multiple-resource rule under RFC8707-2-5. The MUST-level modal inventory does not derive separate sites for these advisory clauses.

Section 2.1 states that an authorization server unable to parse or accept the supplied resources should reject the request with invalid_target. The historical section-3 ID records this lowercase recommendation, whose actual citation remains Section 2.1.

Section 2 permits including the resource parameter with MAY. Section 2.2 states: When the resource parameter is used on an access token request made to the token endpoint, for all grant types, it indicates the target service or protected resource where the client intends to use the requested access token. The retained permission row now cites Sections 2 and 2.2 rather than Section 4, which concerns privacy.

IANA Considerations. No site: the section registers parameters and binds no implementer. The two JWT audience rows once filed here state RFC 7519 Section 4.1.3, and were retired under owner decision D-10 (rfc/corrections/rfc8707.md).

sites.quote: Its value MUST be an absolute URI, as specified by Section 4.3 of [RFC3986].
The URI MUST NOT include a fragment component.
